reason: A recorded measurement, no behaviour change. We hoped to drop one of the two outside services Nora uses to read Instagram, because that one has been refusing every request for a profile all day while the same account works normally in a browser. The theory was that it was being refused for looking like a scraper, and that asking with the credentials Nora already uses for messages would be answered instead. It was not — asking the same way Nora reads messages got refused identically, with a properly formed request. So the two-service split stands, and this is written down so nobody spends the same day on it again. One avenue is left untested and needs a change to an outside library rather than an experiment. The practical cost is small: what remains unreadable is whether an account is private and how many followers it has, and Instagram already enforces who may see what against Nora's own login — she never needed to read those to decide, only to explain.
